Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Spellcrafter is a card drafting game where players select letters and special modifier cards to spell the most valuable words across four rounds. Bonus points are awarded for word length and for staying in a single suit. Contents 1 How to play 2 Scoring 3 Game End 4 Wordlist 5 Notes How to play At the start of each round, each player is dealt a hand of 8 cards. One card is then dealt face up to the center of the table: this is a shared letter known as the jumper card. Players look at the cards in their hand and select one card to keep by placing it in a pile face down in front of them. Once everyone has selected a card, players pass their remaining cards to the player on their left, face down. Players repeat this process until they have a pile of 7 selected cards. The final card in each players' hand is discarded instead of drafted. Once drafting is complete, players must each craft a word of three or more letters using some or all of their selected cards and the jumper shared card. It is not mandatory to use the jumper or special cards. Each player then scores points for the cards they used to craft their word (plus any bonuses), then discards all cards face-up to create a discard pile beside the deck. To begin a new round, a new hand of 8 cards is dealt to each player from the remaining deck and a new jumper card to the middle of the table. Alternate passing direction with each round. If the draw deck runs out of cards while dealing, the entire deck is reshuffled along with any discarded cards. Scoring Each letter has a point value on the top left of the card. Simply add up the value of each letter to determine the value of the word. Flush: Double the word value when all letters are the same suit. Straight: Double the word value when the word is 5 letters or longer. Both: Triple the word value for Straight Flushes! Game End When a player plays a single word worth 50 or more points, that player immediately wins the game, regardless of any other scoring. Otherwise, the game ends after four rounds, and the player with highest total across all four rounds is the winner! If there is a tie, the player with the longest word in the final round wins. Wordlist The list of allowed words for Spellcrafter on BGA is from the Wordnik Wordlist open source project ( full wordlist ). This list is in English and largely excludes proper nouns. Notes Usability Tip: If the Spellcrafter game UI appears small and you're playing in a desktop browser, increasing browser Zoom (often with Ctrl + + ) to a level around 150% may help. Automatic scaling should be addressed in a future update and render this workaround uncessary. [Rating: 4/10] FIRST IMPRESSION:  With Paperback and Hardback available, I see little reason to play this one unless you're looking for something very simple and straightforward. I do wonder just how often it is likely that playing a word in the same suit is more valuable than just playing a longer word. In our game, we didn't see anyone play a word all of the same suit as it was never worth it.

[Rating: 6/10] Decent simple game, but I wish that the green and blue suites weren't so dark, they're a little too close to the black color. I think the scoring could be revised a bit to made tighter, but nothing some house rules can't fix. Overall, still a fun experience I'd recommend for 4-5 players.

[Rating: 6/10] A small letter-drafting game where you're scoring the numbers on the cards and getting a bonus for 5+ letter words and/or words built from a single suit. A few powerup cards add to that. Okay as a light word game, but I'd generally push for Letterpress instead.

[Rating: 6/10] Nice word game with drafting element, though sometimes, lucky or not, you can get or draft perfect cards at round. I think it is decent game, but my mind sometimes goes blank even on simple words and I cannot figure out what to make of letters I drafted.

[Rating: 7/10] A very simple game, but that is also its strength: It doesn't get in the way of simply spelling long words. I think the deck construction/scoring may be a bit off, however. With four suits, you're unlikely to want to try for the single suit bonus. Perhaps that's there as a handicap mechanism? But even so, I suspect it's not enough.
